proposed.label: Treats zero as not a whole number
proposed.description: The student thinks the whole numbers start at 1, like the natural numbers, so places 0 (or a number equal to 0, such as a zero over a non-zero denominator) among the integers that are not whole numbers.

proposed.label: Calls any negative number an integer
proposed.description: The student sees that the number is negative and concludes it is a negative integer, even when it is a negative fraction or a negative square root that is not a whole value.

proposed.label: Uses perfect squares to locate a cube root
proposed.description: The learner sees that the radicand lies between two perfect squares and concludes that its cube root lies between the roots of those squares, instead of using perfect cubes. For example, 30 is between 25 and 36, so the cube root of 30 is wrongly placed between 5 and 6.

proposed.label: Treats a square root as half of the radicand
proposed.description: The learner believes the square root of a number is about half of it (squaring is doubling), so a surd between n and n + 1 is taken to have a radicand near 2n. For example, the square root of 11 is wrongly placed between 5 and 6 because 11 divided by 2 is 5.5.

proposed.label: Uses perfect cubes to locate a square root
proposed.description: The learner sees that the radicand lies between two perfect cubes and concludes that its square root lies between the roots of those cubes, instead of using perfect squares. For example, 30 is between 27 and 64, so the square root of 30 is wrongly placed between 3 and 4.

proposed.label: Listing the numbers from largest to smallest
proposed.description: The student ranks the numbers correctly but writes them from the largest to the smallest, so the list is in descending order when the question asked for ascending order.

proposed.label: Comparing a whole number with the number under the root sign
proposed.description: The student compares the whole number with the radicand instead of with the root. For example, 7 is judged smaller than $\sqrt{40}$ because 7 < 40, although $\sqrt{40}$ is less than 7. The whole number is then always listed first.

proposed.label: Listing the numbers from largest to smallest
proposed.description: The student ranks the numbers correctly but writes them from the largest to the smallest, so the list is in descending order when the question asked for ascending order.

proposed.label: Leaving two surds in the order given when they lie between the same whole numbers
proposed.description: The student places each surd between two whole numbers, but when two surds lie between the same pair of whole numbers they do not compare the numbers under the root signs, so they leave those two surds in the order they were listed.

proposed.label: Multiplies only the first term of the numerator by the missing factor
proposed.description: When rewriting a fraction over the lowest common denominator, the student multiplies the denominator and the x-term of the numerator by the missing factor but leaves the constant term as it was, as if the factor were not applied to the whole bracket.
